newsitem.title: USA: Pfizer targets 1997 growth 10 pct or more.
newsitem.headline: Pfizer targets 1997 growth 10 pct or more.

text.p: Pfizer Inc said on Tuesday that it plans to spend $2 billion on research and development in 1997, up from $1.7 billion a year ago, as it targets revenue and earnings per share growth of at least 10 percent for the year.
Pfizer reported second-quarter earnings per share of $0.35, compared to $0.31 for the same period in 1996.
The First Call consensus estimate for the second quarter of 1997 was $0.36 per share.
Pfizer said in a news release that foreign exchange reduced its revenue growth by four percentage points for the second quarter, and by three percentage points for the first half of 1997.
The company said results will continue to be adversely affected by the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen and certain key European currencies.

Pfizer's pharmaceutical revenues were up 12 percent for the quarter, led by a 15 percent increase, to $1.1 billion, in the United States. Outside the U.S., this group's sales rose eight percent to $1.0 billion.
Sales of Norvaac were $521 million, up 24 percent, while Cardura sales rose 17 percent to $148 million.
Zithromax sales increased 16 percent to $158 million, Zoloft was up nine percent to $323 million and Zyrtec rose 94 percent to $70 million.
Diflucan sales were down 4 percent to $216 million, the company said.

Pfizer's medical technology group sales were $362 million, up one percent. The animal health group had sales of $314 million, up eight percent, while consumer health group sales rose eight percent to $135 million.
